myth.title: Lymphatic drainage detoxes you and melts fat
myth.claim: Lymphatic drainage pulls toxins out of the body and causes fat or weight loss.
myth.harm_reason: Sources say there is no evidence it causes weight loss and the toxin claims are unfounded. The massage itself is not described as harmful.
myth.match_note: Topic: exact phrase in transcript, caption or on-screen text. Claim: topic matches that also contain one of the claim keywords in transcript or caption.

top_video.quote: ✨ Drainage & Detox: Tapping on your lymph nodes boosts lymphatic flow to clear out toxins and reduce swelling.

quoted.quote: ✨ Drainage & Detox: Tapping on your lymph nodes boosts lymphatic flow to clear out toxins and reduce swelling.

verdict: Claims that lymphatic massage removes toxins are unfounded.
what_is_true: It may temporarily smooth cellulite, but it does not affect weight measured on a scale.
what_is_false: Claims that lymphatic massage removes toxins are unfounded.
Lymphatic drainage does not directly cause weight loss.

sources.title: Lymphatic drainage massage: separating fact from fiction
excerpts: Lymphatic drainage massage does not directly cause weight loss
However, there is no evidence that MLD causes weight loss.
A medical professional can perform MLD safely and effectively.

sources.title: What lymphatic drainage massage actually does for your body
excerpts: The claims that lymphatic massage can get rid of toxins are unfounded as well, adds Rockson.
As far as influencers’ claims that lymphatic drainage can help you lose weight, Rockson says it has nothing to do with weight loss.
Cellulite is fluid retention within fat, so lymphatic drainage can temporarily smooth out cellulite, but it won’t affect body weight as measured on a scale.

sources.title: Effects of manual lymphatic drainage on breast cancer-related lymphedema: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
excerpts: Seven studies assessed the reduction in arm volume, and found no significant difference between the MLD and standard treatment groups, with a weighted mean difference of 75.12 (95% CI, -9.34 to 159.58).
The current evidence from RCTs does not support the use of MLD in preventing or treating lymphedema.
However, clinical and statistical inconsistencies between the various studies confounded our evaluation of the effect of MLD on breast-cancer-related lymphedema.

sources.title: Manual lymphatic drainage treatment for lymphedema: a systematic review of the literature.
sources.publisher: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
excerpts: Some studies reported positive effects of MLD on volume reduction, quality of life and symptom-related outcomes compared with other treatments, while other studies reported no additional benefit of MLD as a component of complex decongestive therapy.
MLD may also provide additional benefits in volume reduction for mild lymphedema.
However, in moderate to severe lymphedema, MLD may not provide additional benefit when combined with complex decongestive therapy.

sources.title: Advances in the prevention and treatment of breast cancer-related lymphedema.
excerpts: Complete decongestive therapy (CDT) remains the standard of care for patients with BCRL.
Among CDT components, facilitating manual lymphatic drainage (MLD) using indocyanine green fluorescence lymphography has been proposed.

Reconstructive microsurgical techniques such as lymphovenous anastomosis and vascular lymph node transfer are growing surgical considerations for patients as well as liposuction-based procedures for addressing fatty fibrosis formation from chronic lymphedema.
